identity.name: SARVESHWAR FOODS LIMITED
identity.industry: Food & Beverage / Premium Organic Rice & FMCG

summary.oneLiner: Q1FY26 saw strong revenue growth (29% YoY) and explosive PAT growth (120% YoY) driven by higher-margin organic and FMCG products under Nimbark, with export expansion and retail scaling as key future levers; margin expansion is sustainable due to value-added product mix and global brand ambitions.

one-line thesis: Q1FY26 saw strong revenue growth (29% YoY) and explosive PAT growth (120% YoY) driven by higher-margin organic and FMCG products under Nimbark, with export expansion and retail scaling as key future levers; margin expansion is sustainable due to value-added product mix and global brand ambitions.
financial scorecard: revenue: 301 Cr (+29% YoY); EBITDA: 17.13 Cr (+36% YoY); EBITDA margin: 5.68% (+50% YoY); PAT (reported): 7.02 Cr (+120% YoY); PAT (normalized): 7.02 Cr (no major one-offs); order book: not disclosed; net debt: not disclosed (but Rs. 130 Cr of Rs. 150 Cr rights issue targeted for working capital de-leverage)
guidance: revenue growth: 30%+ CAGR expected; margin: expected to improve further due to organic/FMCG mix; order inflow: not specified; capex/commissioning: no capex planned; focus on working capital and depot expansion in US/EU
segment / subsidiary detail: Domestic revenue: ~85%; Export revenue: ~15%; Nimbark/Himalayan Bio-Organic contribution: ~25% of total revenue (Rs. 70 Cr in Q1, ~Rs. 250 Cr annualized); organic segment has highest margins; Basmati exports to US/EU via private labels; FMCG/ready-to-cook products driving margin uplift
growth verticals / optionality: Global retail brand launch via US/EU depots; scaling Nimbark retail stores from 6 to pan-India; e-commerce expansion; potential entry into Walmart/Whole Foods via existing USFDA/EU certifications
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin improved to 5.68% due to higher mix of organic/FMCG products (higher gross margins); cost pressures mitigated by premium pricing and value addition; export margins currently low (7-8%) but expected to rise to 20-35% with direct depot model
capex / expansion: no capex planned; growth driven by procurement scaling and working capital, not new plants
capital allocation: Rs. 150 Cr rights issue; Rs. 130 Cr allocated to reduce working capital cycle (currently 170-180 days); remaining Rs. 20 Cr for general corporate purposes; no allocation to capex or M&A
risks & watch-items: US tariff volatility on Basmati rice; supply chain delays for export shipments; dependency on Himalayan sourcing region; retail expansion execution risk; working capital intensity remains high
management quality / tone: Highly confident and bullish; emphasis on long-term global brand building; clear articulation of export strategy with depots; strong focus on organic/FMCG as margin drivers; tone is execution-oriented and visionary
non-obvious takeaways: Himalayan Bio-Organic subsidiary is already contributing Rs. 250 Cr annually — implying it's nearly 1/4th of group revenue, yet not separately listed or tracked by market; Nimbark’s organic products (saffron, walnuts, rajma) are globally recognized Himalayan specialties with high export potential beyond rice

themes.title: Agri value-chain - food processing, dairy, protein & seeds
themes.need: Rising protein/processed-food consumption, animal-nutrition demand and export tailwinds drive an integrated agri value-chain - DODLA/PARAGMILK on dairy; AVANTIFEED/SHINDL/SKMEGGPROD/HMAAGRO on aqua/poultry/meat protein; GODREJAGRO/KSCL/NATHBIOGEN on feed + seeds; REGAAL/SUKHJITS/GULPOLY on maize/starch; FOODSIN/MANORAMA on agri-processing & specialty fats.
themes.driver: Monsoon-led farm income; protein export demand; feed-margin recovery; festive processed-food restocking.
